newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russian minister arrives for key NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister arrives for key NATO talks.

text.p: Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov arrived at NATO headquarters on Wednesday for a meeting which could pave the way to a radical new relationship between Russia and the western military alliance.

NATO is hoping Rodionov will take the first concrete step towards a charter between the former cold war enemies after foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov last week said Moscow was ready to talk despite opposition to NATO's eastwards enlargement plans.
That small step at a meeting with defence ministers from the 16-nation alliance would be an agreement to exchange military liaison officers between Russian and NATO political and defence commands.

"We are hoping that he will come up with something, at least this small step," one top NATO official told Reuters. The official indicated that if he did not, it would be due to internal politicking at home rather than hostility towards NATO.
Rodionov, wearing a grey suit after being transferred from the military to civilian life last week, gave little away as he nodded curtly at reporters on arrival.

Russia is deeply opposed to NATO plans, at a July 8-9 summit in Madrid next year, to open talks to admit a number of countries from behind the Iron Curtain. The most likely countries are Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.

NATO is adamant enlargement will go ahead, but wants it accompanied by historic new pacts with Russia and Ukraine and an internal agreement on reform of the alliance's command structure to equip it for more Bosnia-style peace missions.

On Wednesday NATO defence ministers agreed to bolster the so-called Partnership of Peace programme with eastern Europe, in which they take part in peacekeeping missions, to console those who will not join NATO in the first wave.
"The partnership for peace continues to play a dynamic and important role in the development of a new security architecture," the ministers said in a statement.
The talks between Rodionov and NATO will also focus on Bosnia.

Ties have been boosted by Russian participation and help in planning a Stabilisation Force to Bosnia aimed at ensuring the country does not slip back into war after December 20 when the mandate of the current force expires.
The planned charter on offer from NATO would cover every aspect of ties between Russia and the alliance.
NATO Secretary General Javier Solana was authorised by alliance foreign ministers last week to open talks with Russia on the charter which NATO wants to sign at next July's summit.
German Foreign Minister Volker Ruehe said Solana would hold the first round of negotiations in Moscow on January 19-20.
NATO officials now see it as inaugurating a new security order for a post-Cold War Europe which will guarantee peace on the continent well into the next century.
